title: Prompt photon production in a bremsstrahlung in proton-proton collisions at $\sqrt{\mathbf{s}}$=10 GeV NICA energies
summary:
The dependence of differential cross-section of prompt photon production in bremsstrahlung \(qq \rightarrow qqγ\) at collisions of nonpolarized and longitudinally polarized protons at \(\sqrt{s}\)=10 GeV NICA energies on the kinematic parameters: sum of energy of the colliding protons \(\sqrt{s}\), the transverse momentum \emph{p\textsubscript{T}}, the cosine of the scattering angle \emph{Cos(θ)}, the rapidity \emph{y} of photon and \emph{x\textsubscript{T}} has been investigated.
  Differential cross-section of bremsstrahlung accounts for 0.03\% of the total diferential cross section for the production of prompt photons in a proton-proton collisions at NICA entrgies. The polarization of protons has a large influence on the differential cross-section of bremsstrahlung \(qq \rightarrow qqγ\), at large values of the transverse momentum of prompt photons.
  Double spin asymmetry of process of bremsstrahlung on the kinematic parameters has been studied.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates the differential cross-section of prompt photon production via bremsstrahlung (qq → qqγ) in proton-proton collisions at √s = 10 GeV (NICA energies). The bremsstrahlung contribution accounts for ~0.03% of the total prompt photon cross-section. Proton polarization significantly affects the cross-section at high transverse momentum. The study also examines double spin asymmetry as a function of various kinematic parameters.
AI.motivation: To understand the role of bremsstrahlung processes in prompt photon production at NICA energies and to study the influence of proton polarization on the differential cross-section and double spin asymmetry.
AI.method: The differential cross-section of the bremsstrahlung process qq → qqγ is calculated for both nonpolarized and longitudinally polarized proton collisions at √s = 10 GeV. The dependence on kinematic parameters: √s, pT, cos(θ), rapidity y, and xT is analyzed. Double spin asymmetry is also computed.
AI.result: Bremsstrahlung contributes only ~0.03% of the total prompt photon differential cross-section in pp collisions at NICA energies. Proton polarization has a strong influence at large transverse momentum values.
AI.conclusion: While bremsstrahlung is a minor contributor to prompt photon production, its double spin asymmetry and polarization dependence at high pT may provide useful insights for spin physics at NICA energies.

title: The Mass Gap Approach to QCD. II. The non-perturbative renormalization program for the massive gluon fields
summary: We present a non-perturbative multiplicative renormalization program for the massive gluon fields. This has been done within the previously formulated the mass gap approach to QCD. It is based on a new insights into its ground state true dynamical and gauge structures. Our approach makes it possible for gluons to acquire mass dynamically. The corresponding full gluon propagator has been investigated in full details. Its asymptotic properties have been analysed, including the perturbation theory limit. The peculiarities of the mass-shell structure of the full massive gluon propagator has been discussed. The inconsistency of the canonical gauge in QCD is fixed. Our approach does not allow the massive gluons to be the mass-shell objects. This prevents them to appear in the physical spectrum (confinement of massive gluon states). The massive gluons may exist in the vacuum or inside hadrons only. Expressions in Euclidean metric for the lattice simulations are also present. We have also shown that the massive solution has a correct limit to the free massless gluon propagator, when the exactly defined gluon pole mass is to be formally put zero.

AI.tldr: A non-perturbative multiplicative renormalization program for massive gluon fields is developed within the mass gap approach to QCD, showing that gluons acquire mass dynamically while remaining confined (not appearing as mass-shell objects in the physical spectrum). The approach fixes inconsistencies in canonical gauge and provides Euclidean expressions for lattice simulations.
AI.motivation: To develop a non-perturbative renormalization framework for massive gluons within QCD, addressing the inconsistency of canonical gauge and the need to understand the true dynamical and gauge structure of the QCD ground state.
AI.method: Multiplicative renormalization program for massive gluon fields formulated within the mass gap approach to QCD, analyzing the full gluon propagator, its asymptotic properties, mass-shell structure, and the zero-mass limit.
AI.result: Gluons acquire mass dynamically; the full gluon propagator is analyzed in detail; canonical gauge inconsistency is fixed; massive gluons cannot be mass-shell objects and thus do not appear in the physical spectrum (confinement); the massive solution correctly limits to the free massless gluon propagator when pole mass is set to zero; Euclidean metric expressions are provided for lattice simulations.
AI.conclusion: The approach provides a consistent non-perturbative description of massive gluons that are confined (exist only in vacuum or inside hadrons), resolving gauge inconsistency and connecting to perturbation theory and lattice QCD.

title: Echoes of Nucleon Decay from Long-Lived Particles
summary: Nucleon decay searches provide uniquely sensitive probes of baryon number violation and physics beyond the Standard Model. We propose a new class of nucleon decay observables involving long-lived particles (LLPs), characterized by spatially separated but temporally correlated "echo" vertices not captured by conventional prompt searches. Focusing on vector LLPs, we construct effective operators and ultraviolet realizations, and show that Super-Kamiokande, Hyper-Kamiokande and JUNO can achieve geometric acceptances approaching 80% over a broad range of LLP decay lengths. Echo signatures could in principle arise from any visibly decaying LLP.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes "echo" signatures for nucleon decay searches involving long-lived particles (LLPs), where spatially separated but temporally correlated vertices are detected. Focusing on vector LLPs, effective operators and UV realizations are constructed. Detectors like Super-Kamiokande, Hyper-Kamiokande, and JUNO can achieve ~80% geometric acceptance for a wide range of LLP decay lengths.
AI.motivation: Nucleon decay searches are sensitive probes of baryon number violation and beyond-Standard Model physics. Conventional prompt searches may miss signatures involving long-lived particles, motivating the proposal of new "echo" observables.
AI.method: The authors construct effective operators and ultraviolet realizations for vector LLP scenarios. They analyze geometric acceptance for neutrino detectors (Super-Kamiokande, Hyper-Kamiokande, JUNO) using echo signatures—spatially separated but temporally correlated vertices from LLP decays.
AI.result: Geometric acceptances approaching 80% can be achieved over a broad range of LLP decay lengths in the considered detectors.
AI.conclusion: Echo signatures offer a promising new channel for nucleon decay searches involving any visibly decaying long-lived particle, extending sensitivity beyond conventional prompt searches.

title: Precision physics at the muon collider: $m_W$ and CKM matrix elements
summary: We examine the potential for a 10~TeV lepton collider to carry out precision measurements of the W boson mass and W boson couplings strength, i.e. the CKM matrix elements. We consider the several W boson production mechanisms and focus on the most copious at 10~TeV, that is effective $γW \to W$, a process viable at both opposite sign and same-sign leptonic colliders. We find that the leptonic W decay channel can hardly be competitive with present determinations, due to lack of rate. The hadronic channel has potential to improve over the current $\simeq$10~MeV from measurements at hadron colliders, motivating detector developments towards high-precision hadronic energy measurements. We find that the precision understanding of the detector response to hadrons can also lead to a determination of the CKM matrix elements. We expect determination of CKM matrix elements surpassing by far the present precision for couplings involving heavy quarks, notably $V_{cb}$, avoiding the present bottle-necks due to poor knowledge of hadronic matrix elements needed in low energy extractions of CKM matrix elements. Our findings motivate detector developments towards high-precision hadronic energy measurements and flavor tagging.

AI.tldr: This paper examines the potential of a 10 TeV lepton collider to precisely measure the W boson mass and CKM matrix elements via the γW → W production process, finding that hadronic channels could improve W mass precision beyond current ~10 MeV and significantly enhance CKM determinations (especially Vcb), motivating detector developments for high-precision hadronic energy measurements and flavor tagging.
AI.motivation: To explore whether a 10 TeV lepton collider can improve precision measurements of the W boson mass and CKM matrix elements beyond current capabilities, particularly addressing bottlenecks in heavy quark CKM extraction due to poor knowledge of hadronic matrix elements.
AI.method: Analyzes W boson production mechanisms at 10 TeV, focusing on the most copious process γW → W. Evaluates both leptonic and hadronic W decay channels for their potential in mass and coupling measurements, comparing to existing precision from hadron colliders.
AI.result: Leptonic W decay channel is not competitive due to low rate. Hadronic channel can improve over current ~10 MeV W mass precision. CKM matrix element determinations, especially Vcb, can surpass current precision by avoiding hadronic matrix element uncertainties that limit low-energy extractions.
AI.conclusion: The findings motivate detector development toward high-precision hadronic energy measurements and flavor tagging for future 10 TeV lepton colliders.

title: Chiral Electromagnetic Surface Waves on Chern-Simons Interfaces
summary: We show that Maxwell theory with a codimension-$1$ Chern-Simons interface supports chiral electromagnetic surface waves on the interface, even when the bulk theory on both sides is conventional vacuum electrodynamics in infinite space. Solving the exact boundary value problem we find that the Chern-Simons interaction acts with opposite sign on the two helicities oriented along the interface, giving rise to one normalizable mode localized on the interface. This mode is a gapless chiral surface photon with linear dispersion and a frequency-independent index of refraction set by the Chern-Simons coefficient. This mode exists despite the absence of ambient material response or geometric confinement.

AI.tldr: Maxwell theory with a codimension-1 Chern-Simons interface supports a gapless chiral surface photon mode localized on the interface, even in bulk vacuum without material response or confinement.
AI.motivation: To demonstrate that chiral electromagnetic surface waves can arise solely from a Chern-Simons interface term in Maxwell theory, without requiring any bulk material response or geometric confinement.
AI.method: Solving the exact boundary value problem for Maxwell theory with a codimension-1 Chern-Simons interface in infinite vacuum.
AI.result: The Chern-Simons interaction acts with opposite sign on the two helicities oriented along the interface, producing one normalizable, gapless chiral surface photon with linear dispersion and a frequency-independent index of refraction determined by the Chern-Simons coefficient.
AI.conclusion: Chiral surface photons exist as exact solutions in this setup despite the absence of any ambient material or geometric confinement, purely due to the topological Chern-Simons coupling on the interface.

title: Cosmological Collider in the Grassmannian
summary: We revisit the computation of four-point wavefunction coefficients for external conformally coupled scalars exchanging a particle of general mass and spin. Much of the phenomenology of cosmological collider physics in the near-de Sitter limit follows from this function. Computing it in detail is a central challenge in the cosmological bootstrap. Using the cosmological Grassmannian, we write this correlator in closed form using hypergeometric functions and Legendre polynomials. We achieve this by writing the standard bootstrap differential equation using the Plücker coordinates of the Grassmannian, and using the basis of Mandelstam invariants. The correlator in the s-channel can be written in terms of a hypergeometric function of the S Mandelstam, while the spin information appears as an overall Legendre polynomial factor that also depends on the other Mandelstams. We fix the boundary conditions by first demanding the absence of unphysical singularities, and by further matching to kinematic limits of the momentum-space wavefunction. Our formulae in Grassmannian space are much simpler than their counterparts in momentum space, demonstrating another useful application of the Grassmannian as a kinematic space for cosmology.

AI.tldr: The paper computes four-point wavefunction coefficients for conformally coupled scalars exchanging massive particles of general spin, using the cosmological Grassmannian to derive closed-form expressions with hypergeometric functions and Legendre polynomials, simplifying the computation compared to momentum-space approaches.
AI.motivation: Computing four-point wavefunction coefficients is a central challenge in the cosmological bootstrap, as they underlie much of the phenomenology of cosmological collider physics in the near-de Sitter limit.
AI.method: The authors use the cosmological Grassmannian with Plücker coordinates and Mandelstam invariants to write the bootstrap differential equation. The s-channel correlator is expressed as a hypergeometric function of the S Mandelstam, with spin information encoded in a Legendre polynomial factor depending on other Mandelstams. Boundary conditions are fixed by requiring no unphysical singularities and matching momentum-space kinematic limits.
AI.result: Closed-form expressions for the four-point correlator are obtained in Grassmannian space, which are much simpler than their momentum-space counterparts.
AI.conclusion: The Grassmannian provides a useful kinematic space for cosmology, simplifying computations that are otherwise challenging in momentum space.

title: The Higgs-top-$Z$ mass coincidence relation after NNLO matching
summary: The relation $M_H^2\simeq M_ZM_t$, previously proposed as a non-trivial Higgs mass coincidence, is reconsidered with present electroweak inputs and with a scheme-consistent matching analysis. With the 2025 PDG values for $M_Z$, $M_W$ and $M_H$, and the ATLAS-CMS direct top-mass combination, the pole-level ratio is $ρ_{Zt}=M_ZM_t/M_H^2=1.00362\pm0.00261$. Thus an exact pole-level geometric relation predicts either $M_H=125.426\pm0.120\,\mathrm{GeV}$ or $M_t=171.898\pm0.302\,\mathrm{GeV}$, which is still a $1.4σ$ test rather than an exclusion. By contrast, the companion arithmetic relation gives $ρ_{Wt}=(M_W+M_t)/(2M_H)=1.00994\pm0.00159$ and is not a viable exact mass sum rule. We then evaluate the complete NNLO weak-scale $\overline{\mathrm{MS}}$ matching formulae at $μ=M_t$. In the standard convention one obtains $\widehatρ_{Zt}(M_t)=\sqrt{g_2^2+g_Y^2}\,y_t/(4\sqrt2λ)=0.96714\pm0.00361$. Consequently, the exact running-coupling boundary condition $λ=g_Zy_t/(4\sqrt2)$ at the top scale would predict $M_H=123.19\pm0.20\,\mathrm{GeV}$, or equivalently $M_t=177.81\pm0.50\,\mathrm{GeV}$ when $M_H$ is held fixed. This is incompatible with the measured point. A possible symmetry explanation must therefore act on pole-level threshold quantities, or provide a finite matching factor $κ_{\rm th}=1.0340\pm0.0039$ at the electroweak scale. We formulate this requirement as a target for custodial/top-Higgs or triality-like symmetry extensions.

AI.tldr: This paper re-examines the Higgs mass coincidence relation $M_H^2 \simeq M_Z M_t$ using current PDG data and scheme-consistent matching, finding it still holds at 1.4σ at pole level but fails at the $\overline{\mathrm{MS}}$ level, requiring a threshold correction factor $\kappa_{\mathrm{th}} = 1.0340 \pm 0.0039$ if a symmetry explanation is invoked.
AI.motivation: To test whether the previously proposed geometric relation $M_H^2 \simeq M_Z M_t$ between the Higgs, Z boson, and top quark masses remains viable with updated electroweak inputs and proper renormalization scheme matching, and to explore possible symmetry-based explanations.
AI.method: Using 2025 PDG values for $M_Z$, $M_W$, $M_H$, and the ATLAS-CMS combined top mass, the authors compute pole-level ratios $\rho_{Zt}$ and $\rho_{Wt}$, and compare them to exact geometric/arithmetic relations. They then perform a complete NNLO $\overline{\mathrm{MS}}$ matching analysis at $\mu = M_t$, converting to running couplings to test the boundary condition $\lambda = g_Z y_t / (4\sqrt{2})$.
AI.result: The pole-level ratio $\rho_{Zt} = 1.00362 \pm 0.00261$ is consistent with unity at 1.4σ. The arithmetic relation $\rho_{Wt} = 1.00994 \pm 0.00159$ deviates more significantly. At the $\overline{\mathrm{MS}}$ level, $\widehat{\rho}_{Zt}(M_t) = 0.96714 \pm 0.00361$, incompatible with unity, implying a needed threshold correction factor $\kappa_{\mathrm{th}} = 1.0340 \pm 0.0039$ for a symmetry-based explanation.
AI.conclusion: The pole-level geometric relation remains viable as a coincidence at 1.4σ, but the running-coupling analysis rules out an exact symmetry at the $\overline{\mathrm{MS}}$ level without finite threshold corrections. A symmetry explanation must act on pole-level thresholds or introduce a $\kappa_{\mathrm{th}}$ factor, pointing toward custodial/top-Higgs or triality-like symmetry extensions.

title: Multipositivity Constrains the Chiral Lagrangian
comment: 10 pages, 2 figures. Ancillary files: Amplitudes and explanatory readme
summary: The chiral Lagrangian is a cornerstone of modern particle physics, offering a systematic and quantitative description of low-energy pions. Using tools from the modern scattering amplitudes program, we show that consistent multiparticle dynamics impose novel constraints on the coupling constants of this theory. In the planar limit, these constraints imply that certain Wilson coefficients of the chiral Lagrangian are bounded from below by the chiral anomaly. Our results reveal a subtle connection between the anomalous and nonanomalous sectors of the underlying strong interactions, while introducing a novel formulation of multipositivity bounds that holds for any planar tree-level theory.

AI.tldr: Using scattering amplitudes techniques, the authors show that consistent multiparticle dynamics impose new constraints on chiral Lagrangian couplings, and in the planar limit, certain Wilson coefficients are bounded below by the chiral anomaly, revealing a connection between anomalous and nonanomalous sectors.
AI.motivation: To uncover novel constraints on the chiral Lagrangian's coupling constants from consistent multiparticle dynamics, and to reveal a subtle connection between the anomalous and nonanomalous sectors of strong interactions.
AI.method: Employ tools from the modern scattering amplitudes program to analyze consistent multiparticle dynamics in the planar limit, deriving lower bounds on Wilson coefficients and formulating multipositivity bounds for planar tree-level theories.
AI.result: Certain Wilson coefficients of the chiral Lagrangian are bounded from below by the chiral anomaly in the planar limit; a novel formulation of multipositivity bounds is introduced that holds for any planar tree-level theory.
AI.conclusion: The results establish a subtle connection between the anomalous and nonanomalous sectors of strong interactions, and introduce a general framework for multipositivity bounds applicable to planar tree-level theories.

title: Deep Neural Networks for Heavy Lepton-Flavor-Violating Higgs Searches at the LHC
summary: We study lepton-flavor-violating (LFV) decays of a heavy Higgs boson, $H \to μτ$, in the Type-III two-Higgs-doublet model by recasting the CMS search at $\sqrt{s} = 13$ TeV with 35.9 fb$^{-1}$ using fast detector simulation in the mass range 200-450 GeV. We develop a deep neural network (DNN) classifier trained on final-state kinematic variables that, with mass-dependent threshold optimization, reduces the expected 95% CL upper limits on the signal cross section by 42-46% in the 0-jet channel and 36-40% in the 1-jet channel relative to the standard collinear mass ($M_\mathrm{col}$) baseline. We apply SHAP interpretability analysis to identify the visible mass $m_\mathrm{vis}$ as one of the dominant discriminating feature, reflecting the characteristic neutrino momentum fraction of the $τ$ decay. We show that supplementing the $M_\mathrm{col}$ analysis with a simplified mass-dependent pre-selection, $m_\mathrm{vis} < f \cdot m_H$ with $f = 0.7$ (0-jet) and $f = 0.8$ (1-jet), consistently improves the sensitivity over the $M_\mathrm{col}$-only baseline without requiring multivariate infrastructure. In addition, a DNN regression model trained to predict the ratio $m_H/M_\mathrm{col}$ corrects the systematic prediction bias inherent in the collinear approximation, maintaining an absolute mass prediction error below 1 GeV for signals up to 400 GeV and improving the mass resolution by 12% (0-jet) and 21% (1-jet) at $m_H = 450$ GeV. These results demonstrate a clear path toward significantly enhanced sensitivity in LFV Higgs searches at the LHC.

AI.tldr: This paper studies lepton-flavor-violating Higgs decays H→μτ in the Type-III 2HDM, using a DNN classifier with mass-dependent threshold optimization to reduce CMS 95% CL upper limits by 42-46% (0-jet) and 36-40% (1-jet) versus the M_col baseline, and a DNN regression model that corrects collinear approximation bias to <1 GeV mass prediction error.
AI.motivation: To improve sensitivity in searches for lepton-flavor-violating Higgs decays (H→μτ) at the LHC, which are key probes of new physics beyond the Standard Model, by overcoming the limitations of the standard collinear mass (M_col) analysis.
AI.method: Recast of CMS 13 TeV search with 35.9 fb⁻¹ using fast detector simulation; DNN classifier trained on final-state kinematic variables with mass-dependent threshold optimization; SHAP interpretability; DNN regression model to correct M_col bias; simplified mass-dependent pre-selection m_vis < f·m_H.
AI.result: DNN classifier reduces expected 95% CL upper limits by 42-46% (0-jet) and 36-40% (1-jet) vs. M_col baseline. SHAP identifies m_vis as key discriminant. Simplified pre-selection (f=0.7/0.8) consistently improves sensitivity. DNN regression corrects bias to <1 GeV error and improves mass resolution by 12% (0-jet) and 21% (1-jet) at m_H=450 GeV.
AI.conclusion: The proposed methods provide a clear path to significantly enhanced sensitivity in LFV Higgs searches at the LHC, with both advanced multivariate and simplified approaches offering substantial improvements over the standard analysis.

title: Algebraic locality and non-invertible Gauss laws
summary: We study algebraic locality principles on a 2+1D closed lattice in the presence of a Gauss law for a non-invertible symmetry. Prior work in arXiv:2509.03589 showed that when enforcing the Gauss law of an invertible symmetry, the principle of "Haag duality" is preserved exactly, and "disjoint additivity" is preserved after appropriate treatment of discreteness artifacts. Here we show that for a large class of non-invertible on-site symmetries, Haag duality is preserved exactly only for sufficiently nice, "cuspless" regions. For cusped regions, we instead have a weak form of Haag duality that requires adding a collar. Our results apply to double models with a purely magnetic constraint, and to the more general framework of constraints induced by the on-site action of a Hopf algebra. In particular, we treat a class of extended string-net models explicitly. We also demonstrate disjoint additivity for double models based on a group, and a weakened form of disjoint additivity in the setting of a general Hopf algebra.

AI.tldr: This paper studies locality principles (Haag duality and disjoint additivity) for non-invertible symmetries on 2+1D lattices with Gauss law constraints, finding that Haag duality holds exactly only for cuspless regions (requiring a collar for cusped regions) and that disjoint additivity holds for group-based double models but is weakened for general Hopf algebra settings.
AI.motivation: To understand how locality principles (Haag duality and disjoint additivity) behave under non-invertible symmetry constraints, extending prior work that treated invertible symmetries (arXiv:2509.03589).
AI.method: Analytical study of algebraic locality on 2+1D closed lattices with Gauss laws for non-invertible symmetries, applied to double models with purely magnetic constraints, constraints from Hopf algebra on-site actions, and extended string-net models.
AI.result: Haag duality holds exactly only for cuspless regions; for cusped regions a weak form requiring a collar is obtained. Disjoint additivity holds for group-based double models but only in weakened form for general Hopf algebra settings.
AI.conclusion: Non-invertible symmetries impose nontrivial restrictions on locality principles compared to invertible ones, with cusp geometry playing a key role in determining whether exact or weak Haag duality holds.

title: Semileptonic sum rules in heavy-to-light charm decays
summary: We investigate semileptonic sum rules in heavy-to-light charm decays, motivated by analogous relations in $b \to c$ and $b \to u$ transitions. Focusing on the $c \to d\overline{\ell}ν$ decays, $D \to π\overline{\ell}ν$, $D \to ρ\overline{\ell}ν$, and $Λ_c \to n\overline{\ell}ν$, we examine a relation among their lepton-flavor universality ratios $R_H^{μe}$. Although the charm sum rule is less precise than the relations in bottom-hadron decays, current low-energy and high-$p_T$ constraints on new physics restrict the actual deviation from the relation to below the percent level. The relation can therefore provide a useful consistency check of charm semileptonic measurements. As an application, we derive a prediction for the yet-unmeasured ratio $R_n^{μe}$ in $Λ_c \to n\overline{\ell}ν$.

AI.tldr: The paper examines semileptonic sum rules in charm decays (c→d transitions), analyzing lepton-flavor universality ratios R_H^{μe} for D→π, D→ρ, and Λ_c→n decays. Though less precise than bottom-sector relations, current NP constraints keep deviations below 1%, making it useful for consistency checks. The authors predict the unmeasured R_n^{μe} for Λ_c→n decays.
AI.motivation: To extend semileptonic sum rules, previously studied in b→c and b→u transitions, to charm decays (c→d) and assess their utility for testing lepton-flavor universality and constraining new physics.
AI.method: Analytical derivation of sum rules relating lepton-flavor universality ratios R_H^{μe} across multiple charm semileptonic decay channels (D→π, D→ρ, Λ_c→n), combined with current experimental and theoretical constraints from low-energy and high-pT data.
AI.result: The charm sum rule is less precise than bottom-sector analogs, but existing new physics constraints limit deviations to below the percent level. A prediction for the unmeasured R_n^{μe} in Λ_c→n decays is provided.
AI.conclusion: The charm sum rule serves as a useful consistency check for experimental measurements of semileptonic charm decays, despite its reduced precision relative to bottom-hadron relations.

title: Dissipative stabilization of Ostrogradsky modes in non-equilibrium field theory
summary: In this work, we investigate higher-derivative quantum field theories and the problem of Ostrogradsky instability within an open-system Keldysh-Lindblad framework. Coupling the ghost sector to dissipative baths generates non-perturbative effective masses and dissipative widths through self-consistent gap equations. Above a critical coupling, the nonequilibrium dynamics develops bifurcated dissipative branches, signaling the emergence of a dissipative phase transition and a nontrivial critical structure in parameter space. We find that the resulting dissipative dynamics can suppress ghost excitations through two distinct mechanisms: in one branch, a large dynamically generated effective mass preserves a quasiparticle-like excitation, while in the second branch, strong dissipative broadening destroys the quasiparticle character through overdamped dynamics. Our results suggest that dissipative effects may provide a nonequilibrium mechanism for the spectral suppression of Ostrogradsky ghosts. The comparison with the healthy sector indicates that the stabilization mechanism is intrinsically tied to the ghost-like spectral structure.

AI.tldr: Higher-derivative quantum field theories with Ostrogradsky ghosts are stabilized via an open-system Keldysh-Lindblad framework, where coupling to dissipative baths generates gap equations that produce either a large effective mass (quasiparticle branch) or strong dissipative broadening (overdamped branch), both suppressing ghost excitations above a critical coupling.
AI.motivation: To address the Ostrogradsky instability problem in higher-derivative theories by exploring nonequilibrium dissipative mechanisms rather than conventional conservative approaches, and to understand whether open-system effects can provide spectral suppression of ghost modes.
AI.method: Uses an open-system Keldysh-Lindblad formalism to couple the ghost sector to dissipative baths; solves self-consistent gap equations for effective masses and dissipative widths; analyzes nonequilibrium dynamics and critical behavior in parameter space.
AI.result: Above a critical coupling, bifurcated dissipative branches emerge (dissipative phase transition). Two distinct ghost suppression mechanisms are identified: (1) dynamically generated large effective mass preserving quasiparticle character; (2) strong dissipative broadening leading to overdamped, quasiparticle-destroying dynamics.
AI.conclusion: Dissipative effects offer a viable nonequilibrium mechanism for spectral suppression of Ostrogradsky ghosts, with the stabilization being intrinsically linked to the ghost-like spectral structure rather than generic to all sectors.

title: Symmetry Breaking as Quantum Gate: Entropy and Weak Mixing Angle
summary: We establish a correspondence between two independent entropic probes -- the variation of Rényi mutual information (RMI) across the electroweak symmetry breaking (EWSB) transition and the stabilizer Rényi entropy (SRE) -- in tree-level $2\to 2$ elastic scatterings. After angular averaging, the RMI (helicity basis) and the SRE (fixed beam basis) exhibit identical dependence on $\sin^2θ_W$ within each neutral-current channel. We trace this correspondence to a common physical origin that it's the Yukawa mass insertion acts as a $-\mathrm{i}Y$ quantum gate in chirality space. Minimizing entropies across all processes yields $\sin^2θ_W$ values matching purely axial vector-like couplings in $Z$ boson exchanged channel.

AI.tldr: The paper establishes a correspondence between two entropy measures (Rényi mutual information and stabilizer Rényi entropy) in electroweak scattering processes, showing they share identical dependence on the weak mixing angle sin²θW in neutral-current channels, traced to Yukawa mass insertion acting as a -iY quantum gate in chirality space.
AI.motivation: To uncover a fundamental connection between two independent entropic measures (RMI and SRE) in the context of electroweak symmetry breaking, and to explain the physical origin of this correspondence.
AI.method: The authors compute the variation of Rényi mutual information across the EWSB transition and the stabilizer Rényi entropy for tree-level 2→2 elastic scatterings. They perform angular averaging and compare the dependence on sin²θW in the helicity basis (for RMI) and fixed beam basis (for SRE) across neutral-current channels.
AI.result: The two entropy measures exhibit identical dependence on sin²θW within each neutral-current channel after angular averaging. Minimizing entropies across all processes yields sin²θW values consistent with purely axial vector-like couplings in Z boson exchange channels.
AI.conclusion: The correspondence between RMI and SRE originates from a common mechanism: Yukawa mass insertion acts as a -iY quantum gate in chirality space. Entropy minimization points to axial-vector coupling as a special limit in the Z boson channel.

title: Universalities of Defects in Quantum Field Theories
summary: Defects are both physically rich objects and powerful tools in modern quantum field theory. They are extended operators, such as boundaries, impurities, and probe particles, embedded in many-body systems. In this dissertation, we study the universal aspects of defect dynamics from the perspective of symmetry principles. We bring together several themes, including defect renormalization group flows, effective string theory, and impurities in atomic quantum gases.

AI.tldr: This dissertation studies the universal aspects of defect dynamics in quantum field theory through symmetry principles, covering defect renormalization group flows, effective string theory, and impurities in atomic quantum gases.
AI.motivation: Defects (boundaries, impurities, probe particles) are physically rich objects and powerful tools in modern quantum field theory. The dissertation aims to understand their universal dynamics from the perspective of symmetry principles.
AI.method: The author brings together several themes: defect renormalization group flows, effective string theory, and impurities in atomic quantum gases, unified by the framework of symmetry principles.
AI.result: The dissertation provides a study of universal aspects of defect dynamics across different physical contexts using symmetry principles as the unifying framework.
AI.conclusion: Defect dynamics in quantum field theory exhibit universal aspects that can be systematically understood through symmetry principles, bridging diverse phenomena from high-energy theory to atomic quantum gases.

title: $b\to c \bar u q$ decay and CP violating observables in the presence of new physics contributions
summary: In this work, a comprehensive analysis for processes related to $b\to c\bar{u}q~(q=d, s)$ transitions are carried out, including new physics contributions. In light of a recent tension between branching fractions for $B_{(s)}\to D_{(s)}^{(*)}M$ ($M$ represents a meson) decays in the QCD factorization approach and relevant experimental results, phenomenological constraints on complex-valued Wilson coeffients are discussed. Analyzed observables contain direct CP asymmetry ($A_{\text{CP}}$) in $B^-\to D^0π^-$ decays and $γ/φ_3$, one of the angles in the unitarity triangle, combined with others from $τ_{B^+}/τ_{B_d}$, $ΔΓ_{q}/Γ_q$, and $A_{\rm SL}^{q}~(q=d, s)$. We constrain the complex Wilson coefficients at $1σ$ and $2σ$ levels under color-singlet and color-rearranged scenarios. These constraints yield correlated predictions for $ΔΓ_d/Γ_d$, $A_{\rm SL}^d$ and $A_{\text{CP}}$.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes $b\to c\bar{u}q$ transitions with new physics contributions, constrains complex Wilson coefficients using tensions in QCD factorization predictions vs experimental $B_{(s)}\to D_{(s)}^{(*)}M$ branching fractions, and provides correlated predictions for $ΔΓ_d/Γ_d$, $A_{\rm SL}^d$, and $A_{\text{CP}}$.
AI.motivation: To address the tension between QCD factorization predictions and experimental branching fractions for $B_{(s)}\to D_{(s)}^{(*)}M$ decays, and to constrain new physics via complex Wilson coefficients.
AI.method: Phenomenological constraints on complex-valued Wilson coefficients under color-singlet and color-rearranged scenarios, using observables including $A_{\text{CP}}$ in $B^-\to D^0π^-$, $γ/φ_3$, $τ_{B^+}/τ_{B_d}$, $ΔΓ_{q}/Γ_q$, and $A_{\rm SL}^{q}$.
AI.result: Constraints on complex Wilson coefficients at $1σ$ and $2σ$ levels, leading to correlated predictions for $ΔΓ_d/Γ_d$, $A_{\rm SL}^d$, and $A_{\text{CP}}$.
AI.conclusion: New physics contributions in $b\to c\bar{u}q$ transitions can be constrained by current experimental data, yielding predictive correlations among key observables.

title: Generalised Cartan Geometry
comment: Contribution to the proceedings of the Corfu Summer Institute 2025 "School and Workshops on Elementary Particle Physics and Gravity" (CORFU2025), 27 April - 28 September, 2025
summary: This talk introduces a Cartan-geometric framework for generalised geometries governed by a differential graded Lie algebra. In contrast to ordinary Cartan geometry, the tangent bundle is extended and qu both a global duality group and a local gauge group. This framework provides a systematic construction of generalised connections and their torsion and curvature tensors for generic generalised geometries. We also review the realisation of these algebraic structures on the phase space of branes in M-theory.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a Cartan-geometric framework for generalised geometries based on a differential graded Lie algebra, extending the tangent bundle with both global duality and local gauge groups, and applies it to construct generalised connections, torsion, and curvature tensors, with a review of their realisation on the phase space of branes in M-theory.
AI.motivation: To develop a systematic Cartan-geometric framework for generalised geometries governed by a differential graded Lie algebra, addressing the limitations of ordinary Cartan geometry by extending the tangent bundle and incorporating both global duality and local gauge groups.
AI.method: The work introduces a Cartan-geometric approach where the tangent bundle is extended, and the framework incorporates a global duality group and a local gauge group. Generalised connections, torsion, and curvature tensors are systematically constructed for generic generalised geometries, and these algebraic structures are reviewed in the context of the phase space of branes in M-theory.
AI.result: A systematic framework for constructing generalised connections, torsion, and curvature tensors in generalised geometries, with a consistent algebraic structure realised on the phase space of branes in M-theory.
AI.conclusion: The Cartan-geometric framework provides a unifying approach to generalised geometries, enabling systematic construction of geometric objects and linking them to the phase space dynamics of branes in M-theory.

title: MAcNLOPS for ZZ Pair Production at the LHC
summary: We present an implementation of the MAcNLOPS matching prescription for $pp \to ZZ$ production in a MadGraph5_aMC@NLO + Pythia8 setup. Starting from a standard MC@NLO event sample, negative H events are removed and compensated by a veto applied to the first shower emission of the S events. The implementation is validated against MC@NLO for radiation-sensitive and inclusive diboson observables. Agreement is found up to a rather small power-suppressed contribution affecting the very low-pT region. The method removes all negative H weights with negligible additional computational cost, while negative S weights are left unchanged, showing that MAcNLOPS is a promising alternative to MC@NLO with a reduced fraction of negative weights.

AI.tldr: The paper presents an implementation of the MAcNLOPS matching prescription for pp→ZZ production in a MadGraph5_aMC@NLO + Pythia8 setup, demonstrating that negative H weights can be removed with negligible computational cost and that the method yields results consistent with MC@NLO for most observables, establishing MAcNLOPS as a promising alternative for reducing negative event weights.
AI.motivation: To reduce the fraction of negative weights in MC@NLO simulations, which are problematic for efficient event generation and analysis, by implementing the MAcNLOPS matching prescription for pp→ZZ production.
AI.method: The MAcNLOPS prescription is implemented in a MadGraph5_aMC@NLO + Pythia8 framework for ZZ diboson production. Negative H (hard) events are removed and compensated by a veto applied to the first shower emission of the S (soft) events, while negative S weights are left unchanged.
AI.result: Agreement between MAcNLOPS and standard MC@NLO is found for inclusive diboson observables, with only a small power-suppressed discrepancy in the very low-pT region. All negative H weights are removed with negligible additional computational cost.
AI.conclusion: MAcNLOPS is a promising alternative to MC@NLO that significantly reduces the fraction of negative weights without substantial computational overhead, while preserving agreement for most observables.

title: New mechanism for fermion localization in $f(T,T_G)$-brane
summary: We investigate the localization of fermionic fields in a five-dimensional braneworld scenario within the framework of modified teleparallel gravity described by a general $f(T,T_G)$ function. Considering a non-minimal coupling between a Dirac spinor and the torsional invariants, we derive the effective Schrödinger-like equations governing the Kaluza-Klein modes. We showed that the contribution of the teleparallel Gauss-Bonnet term significantly modifies the effective potentials and, consequently, the localization properties. The zero-mode analysis reveals that only one chiral component can be localized on the brane, with the degree of confinement depending on the chosen model. In the massive sector, the spectrum is continuous, but resonant states arise due to the internal structure of the potentials. Additionally, we employ information-theoretic measures, such as Shannon entropy and relative probability, to quantify the localization mechanism. Our results show that the torsional modifications induce a nontrivial redistribution of information, exhibiting stronger localization. These findings highlight the role of higher-order torsional terms in shaping fermionic localization and resonance structures in braneworld scenarios.

AI.tldr: This paper studies fermion localization in a 5D braneworld within modified teleparallel gravity $f(T,T_G)$, showing that the teleparallel Gauss-Bonnet term modifies effective potentials, enables chiral zero-mode localization, produces resonant massive states, and enhances localization as quantified by Shannon entropy and relative probability.
AI.motivation: To investigate how higher-order torsional modifications, specifically the teleparallel Gauss-Bonnet term, affect the localization of fermionic fields in a braneworld scenario, extending previous analyses beyond standard teleparallel gravity.
AI.method: A 5D braneworld model in $f(T,T_G)$ modified teleparallel gravity with non-minimal coupling between a Dirac spinor and torsional invariants; derivation of effective Schrödinger-like equations for Kaluza-Klein modes; analysis of zero-mode and massive spectra; information-theoretic quantification using Shannon entropy and relative probability.
AI.result: The teleparallel Gauss-Bonnet term significantly modifies effective potentials; only one chiral component of the zero mode is localized; the massive spectrum is continuous with resonant states; Shannon entropy and relative probability reveal stronger localization and nontrivial information redistribution due to torsional modifications.
AI.conclusion: Higher-order torsional terms play a crucial role in shaping fermionic localization and resonance structures in braneworld scenarios, providing a richer framework for addressing fermion confinement.

title: Equation of State at High Baryon Densities from a Thermodynamically Informed Neural Network
comment: 9 pages, 5 figures; feedback is greatly appreciated. The reader is encouraged to test the equation of state in their hydrodynamic codes. Feel free to reach out if you need help with implementation
summary: We present a four-dimensional equation of state for strongly interacting matter at finite temperature and conserved charge densities, constructed using a deep neural network. It is designed for direct use in hybrid models of relativistic heavy-ion collisions: it reproduces hadron resonance gas thermodynamics at typical particlization scales, is consistent with lattice QCD at low baryon chemical potential, and extrapolates into the high-density region inaccessible to either approach, which is precisely the regime targeted by RHIC BES, FAIR, HADES, and CBM. Thermodynamic consistency throughout the full phase space is enforced via a physics-informed loss function. We demonstrate the developed equation of state by implementing it at zero net strangeness and fixed electric-to-baryon charge ratio within the integrated hydrokinetic model.

AI.tldr: A deep neural network-based 4D equation of state for strongly interacting matter is presented, covering finite temperature and conserved charge densities, designed for hybrid heavy-ion collision models with thermodynamic consistency enforced via physics-informed loss functions.
AI.motivation: To construct an equation of state that bridges the gap between hadron resonance gas at low densities, lattice QCD at low baryon chemical potential, and extrapolates into the high-density region inaccessible to either approach, for use in heavy-ion collision simulations at RHIC BES, FAIR, HADES, and CBM.
AI.method: A deep neural network is used to parametrize the 4D equation of state. Thermodynamic consistency across the full phase space is enforced via a physics-informed loss function. The EoS reproduces hadron resonance gas at particlization scales and matches lattice QCD at low baryon chemical potential.
AI.result: The developed equation of state is implemented at zero net strangeness and fixed electric-to-baryon charge ratio within the integrated hydrokinetic model, demonstrating its applicability in hybrid heavy-ion collision simulations.
AI.conclusion: The proposed deep neural network-based EoS successfully unifies different theoretical regimes (HRG, lattice QCD, and extrapolated high-density region) with enforced thermodynamic consistency, providing a practical tool for modeling heavy-ion collisions across a wide range of beam energies.

title: Stochastic inflation as an open quantum system II: open effective field theory and stochastic matching
summary: We further develop the proposal in Phys.\ Rev.\ Lett.\ \textbf{136} 071501 that interprets stochastic inflation as an open quantum system, by constructing the open effective field theory for the reduced density matrix of long wavelength modes. We clarify that this open effective field theory enjoys two renormalization group flows: the conventional Wilsonian channel, and a stochastic channel arising from the openness that has no counterpart in ordinary Wilsonian effective field theory. Focusing on the stochastic channel in the hard cutoff scheme, we identify both Gaussian and non-Gaussian diffusion as effective operators in the influence functional, and show that they are required by matching onto correlators and form factors of the perturbative full theory through a method-of-region in time. Beyond Gaussian order, the matching data are no longer local Wilson coefficients but nonlocal and non-Markovian Wilson kernels. We then obtain the bare Hamiltonian density of this open effective field theory and derive its nonlocal functional master equations, including the Fokker-Planck equation for the diagonal density matrix and the Klein-Kramers equation for the Wigner functional, with their zero-modess simplifications discussed. Finally, we take a first step toward a continuum version of this open effective field theory, replacing the hard cutoff by an analytic regulator in the stochastic channel, and demonstrate stochastic renormalization using a massive scalar as an example.

AI.tldr: This paper extends the interpretation of stochastic inflation as an open quantum system by constructing an open effective field theory (OEFT) for long-wavelength modes. It identifies two renormalization group flows—Wilsonian and stochastic—derives nonlocal functional master equations, and takes initial steps toward continuum regularization and stochastic renormalization.
AI.motivation: To further develop the open quantum system interpretation of stochastic inflation (from Phys. Rev. Lett. 136 071501) by formulating a rigorous open effective field theory framework that captures both Gaussian and non-Gaussian diffusion effects.
AI.method: Constructs an open effective field theory for the reduced density matrix of long-wavelength modes, using a hard cutoff scheme, method-of-region matching in time, and an analytic regulator for continuum generalization.
AI.result: Identifies two RG flows (Wilsonian and stochastic); shows non-Gaussian diffusion requires nonlocal, non-Markovian Wilson kernels; derives functional master equations (Fokker-Planck, Klein-Kramers) and demonstrates stochastic renormalization for a massive scalar.
AI.conclusion: The open EFT framework successfully captures stochastic inflation's dissipative and diffusive dynamics beyond Gaussian order, with implications for non-Markovianity and continuum renormalization in open quantum systems.

title: Probing freeze-in dark matter using Bose-Einstein condensate in neutron star
summary: Neutron star (NS) is one of the most promising astrophysical targets to probe non-gravitational interaction of dark matter (DM) with visible matter. Their compactness makes them an ideal object which can capture particle DM efficiently over its lifetime using the DM-nucleon scattering cross-section. If DM particles are bosonic, then the captured DM population may form a Bose-Einstein condensate at the center of the NS, increasing the DM density significantly. In this work, we study the phenomenology of such scenario with enhanced DM annihilation rate due to the increased density in a condensate. The enhanced DM annihilation makes the NS surface `hotter' than in the standard cooling scenario. We show that the annihilation rate is enhanced by a factor of $\mathcal{O}(10^{15}-10^{20})$ if DM forms a condensate, and DM with freeze-in value annihilation cross-section can heat up the NS to higher temperatures, bringing it within the reach of James Webb Space Telescope. It also allows us to probe DM-nucleon scattering cross section within the neutrino fog regime which will complement the terrestrial direct detection searches. Moreover, the enhanced annihilation from the condensate changes the lower limits on s-wave DM annihilation cross-section for capture-annihilation equilibrium and the formation of a black hole inside the NS. Finally, we show an example of a scalar DM model where such small annihilation and DM-nucleon scattering cross sections can generically arise.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates how bosonic dark matter forming a Bose-Einstein condensate inside neutron stars can dramatically enhance DM annihilation rates (by ~10^15-10^20), heating the neutron star surface to detectable levels by JWST, probing DM-nucleon scattering in the neutrino fog regime, and modifying constraints on DM annihilation cross-sections and black hole formation thresholds.
AI.motivation: Neutron stars are excellent targets for probing non-gravitational DM interactions due to their compactness and efficient DM capture. The authors aim to study the phenomenological consequences when captured bosonic DM forms a Bose-Einstein condensate, which could significantly amplify DM density and annihilation rates beyond standard scenarios.
AI.method: The authors analyze DM capture and condensation in NS cores, compute the enhanced annihilation rate from BEC formation (~10^15-10^20 enhancement factor), derive the resulting NS surface heating, and evaluate observability with JWST. They also reassess capture-annihilation equilibrium conditions and black hole formation constraints in the presence of condensate-enhanced annihilation, and present a concrete scalar DM model realizing the required cross-sections.
AI.result: DM annihilation rate is enhanced by ~10^15-10^20 if DM forms a condensate. Freeze-in scale annihilation cross-sections can heat NS to temperatures detectable by JWST. The scenario probes DM-nucleon scattering cross-sections in the neutrino fog region, complementing direct detection. Enhanced annihilation modifies lower limits on s-wave DM annihilation cross-section for equilibrium and black hole formation.
AI.conclusion: Bose-Einstein condensation of bosonic DM inside NS dramatically boosts annihilation signals, enabling JWST detection and probing parameter space (neutrino fog) inaccessible to terrestrial experiments. This scenario also revises constraints on DM annihilation and black hole formation in NS.

title: Krakow Lectures on Scalar Quantum Solitons
summary: We give a pedagogical introduction to Linearized Soliton Perturbation Theory (LSPT), a new and efficient tool for calculations involving quantum solitons. It is a Hamiltonian approach with a focus on explicitly constructing the soliton states. These states are squeezed, coherent states plus perturbative corrections. We will describe multi-loop corrections to states and their masses. An inner product suitable for non-normalizable momentum eigenstates will be introduced and applied to kink-meson scattering. We will also discuss domain wall solitons.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces Linearized Soliton Perturbation Theory (LSPT), a Hamiltonian-based method for quantum soliton calculations that constructs soliton states as squeezed coherent states with perturbative corrections, covers multi-loop corrections to states and masses, introduces an inner product for non-normalizable momentum eigenstates applied to kink-meson scattering, and discusses domain wall solitons.
AI.motivation: To develop a more efficient and pedagogical Hamiltonian framework (LSPT) for calculating quantum properties of solitons, addressing the need for explicit construction of soliton states beyond traditional methods.
AI.method: Linearized Soliton Perturbation Theory (LSPT) — a Hamiltonian approach that constructs soliton states as squeezed coherent states with perturbative corrections, includes multi-loop corrections, and introduces a specialized inner product for non-normalizable momentum eigenstates.
AI.result: Demonstrates the application of LSPT to kink-meson scattering and domain wall solitons, showing its utility for multi-loop calculations and handling non-normalizable states.
AI.conclusion: LSPT provides a new efficient tool for quantum soliton calculations with explicit state construction and broad applicability to various soliton systems.

title: Entanglement viscosity to entropy density ratio for spin-3/2 theory
summary: It is known that the Minkowski vacuum appears as a thermal medium to an accelerated observer due to the renowned Unruh effect. More recently, it has been shown that at least for lower-spin fields this medium also exhibits a non-zero "entanglement" shear viscosity, which saturates the fundamental Kovtun-Son-Starinets (KSS) bound. We test the universality of this result for higher spins by computing the entanglement viscosity for spin-3/2 fields within the Rarita-Schwinger-Adler (RSA) theory. Strikingly, we obtain a negative viscosity. However, computing the entropy density using the modular Hamiltonian expansion method, we find it is also negative, and the viscosity to entropy ratio saturates the KSS bound. To clarify the origin of the negativity, we use another approach of Zubarev density operator, which gives positive entropy. We also show that RSA theory has many features of a conformal field theory.

AI.tldr: The paper investigates the entanglement shear viscosity for spin-3/2 fields in Rarita-Schwinger-Adler theory, finding negative viscosity and negative entropy density, yet the viscosity-to-entropy ratio still saturates the KSS bound. An alternative Zubarev approach yields positive entropy, and the theory exhibits conformal field theory features.
AI.motivation: To test the universality of the KSS bound saturation for higher-spin fields, specifically spin-3/2, building on earlier results for lower-spin fields that show non-zero entanglement shear viscosity saturating the bound.
AI.method: Computing entanglement viscosity and entropy density for spin-3/2 fields in Rarita-Schwinger-Adler theory using the modular Hamiltonian expansion method, and cross-checking with the Zubarev density operator approach.
AI.result: Negative viscosity and negative entropy density are obtained via the modular Hamiltonian method, yet the viscosity-to-entropy ratio saturates the KSS bound. The Zubarev approach yields positive entropy. RSA theory shows conformal field theory properties.
AI.conclusion: The KSS bound saturation is universal for spin-3/2 fields despite negative values, though the negativity's origin requires further clarification. The modular Hamiltonian and Zubarev approaches give different entropy signs, indicating subtlety in defining thermodynamic quantities for higher-spin fields.

title: Pseudo-Nambu-Goldstone inflation with $Z_N$ symmetric waterfall fields
summary: We propose a hybrid inflation model where a pseudo-Nambu-Goldstone boson inflaton couples to $N$ waterfall scalar fields respecting a $Z_N$ symmetry. We identify the phases for the inflation and the consequent waterfall transition, concretely, in $Z_2$, $Z_3$ and $Z_4$ cases. From the Coleman-Weinberg potential for the inflaton, we show that the quadratically divergent corrections coming from the waterfall sector are cancelled due to the $Z_N$ symmetry, while the logarithmically divergent corrections are absent only for $N>2$, ensuring the radiative stability of the inflaton potential. We show the parameter space for a successful inflation with the loop-corrected inflaton potential in each model and compare the results between different discrete symmetries. We further analyze the vacuum structure of the models and the reheating process due to the $Z_N$-invariant Higgs-portal couplings for the waterfall fields. We find that the reheating temperature can be smaller than the mass of the waterfall field condensate such that the $Z_N$ symmetry is not restored after reheating and there is no domain wall problem in the models. We also comment on the possibility of multi-component dark matter from the $Z_N$ partners of the waterfall field condensate.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a hybrid inflation model with a pseudo-Nambu-Goldstone boson inflaton coupled to N waterfall fields under a Z_N symmetry. It analyzes inflation phases for Z_2, Z_3, Z_4 cases, shows that Z_N symmetry cancels quadratic divergences (and N>2 eliminates logarithmic ones), studies parameter space, vacuum structure, reheating via Higgs-portal couplings (finding reheating temperature below waterfall condensate mass, avoiding domain wall problem), and discusses multi-component dark matter possibilities.
AI.motivation: To construct a radiatively stable hybrid inflation model where the inflaton potential is protected from quantum corrections by a discrete Z_N symmetry, addressing naturalness issues in hybrid inflation scenarios.
AI.method: The authors construct a model coupling a pseudo-Nambu-Goldstone boson inflaton to N waterfall fields via a Z_N symmetry, compute the Coleman-Weinberg potential, analyze divergence cancellation, and perform parameter space scans for Z_2, Z_3, Z_4 cases.
AI.result: Quadratic divergences from waterfall sector are cancelled by Z_N symmetry; logarithmic divergences are absent for N>2. Reheating temperature can be kept below the waterfall condensate mass, preventing Z_N symmetry restoration and domain wall problems. Multi-component dark matter candidates arise from Z_N partners.
AI.conclusion: Z_N discrete symmetries provide a viable framework for radiatively stable hybrid inflation with controlled reheating and no domain wall problem, with potential dark matter implications.

title: Shading A-polynomials via huge representations of $U_q(\mathfrak{su}_N)$
summary: Classical A-polynomials $A(\ell,m)$ define constraints on coordinates $\ell$ and $m$ in $SL(2,\mathbb{C})$ (a complexification of $SU(2)$) character varieties associated to knot complements $S^3\setminus K$. Quantum A-polynomials $\hat A(\hat \ell,\hat m)$ are difference operators annihilating Jones polynomials believed to represent wave functions of 3d Chern-Simons theory with gauge group $SU(2)$ on a toroidal pipe surrounding the knot $K$ strand -- a boundary of the knot complements $S^3\setminus K$. We suggest a construction of classical shaded A-polynomials $A_a(\ell_b,m_c)$ associated to Lie groups $SU(N)$. We exploit a formalism of Clebsh-Gordan (CG) chords, where indices $a$, $b$, $c$ run over $1,\ldots,N-1$. CG chords have a natural interpretation in terms of 2d CFTs of WZW type, or, alternatively, in terms of quantum group $U_q(\mathfrak{su}_N)$. In the case of $\mathfrak{su}_2$ CG chords could be associated to Reeb chords in a knot contact homology (KCH) framework. KCH suggests its own analogue of A-polynomials known as augmentation polynomials allowed to have extra spurious roots in principle. Yet the CG chord formalism could be easily extended to arbitrary $\mathfrak{su}_N$ allowing us to generalize the construction of A(ugmentation)-polynomials to arbitrary $\mathfrak{su}_N$ and arbitrary representation as well. Primarily we aim at classical A-polynomials by considering a double scaling limit when $q=e^{\hbar}$, $\hbar\to 0$ and the representations are huge, in particular, highest weight vector components $w_i\to \infty$ so that $\hbar w_i\sim m_i$ remain finite. Still we expect the presented techniques would be helpful in deriving quantum A-polynomials for arbitrary Lie (super)algebras $\mathfrak{g}$. Also we discuss explicit examples of A-polynomials for knots $3_1$, $4_1$ and $5_1$ for $\mathfrak{g}=\mathfrak{su}_3$.

AI.tldr: The paper extends classical A-polynomials (from $SL(2,\mathbb{C})$ knot theory) to $SU(N)$ via Clebsch-Gordan chords, linking to 2d CFTs, quantum groups $U_q(\mathfrak{su}_N)$, and knot contact homology. It constructs shaded A-polynomials $A_a(\ell_b,m_c)$ and gives explicit examples for $\mathfrak{su}_3$ knots $3_1$, $4_1$, $5_1$, with a double-scaling limit connecting classical and quantum versions.
AI.motivation: To generalize classical and quantum A-polynomials from $SU(2)$ to higher-rank $SU(N)$ gauge groups, using Clebsch-Gordan chords as a unifying framework that bridges knot contact homology, 2d CFTs, and quantum groups.
AI.method: The authors exploit Clebsch-Gordan (CG) chord formalism, where indices run over $1,\ldots,N-1$, and interpret them via WZW-type 2d CFTs or $U_q(\mathfrak{su}_N)$. They consider a double-scaling limit ($q=e^\hbar$, $\hbar\to0$, large representations with $\hbar w_i\sim m_i$ finite) to recover classical A-polynomials from quantum ones.
AI.result: Construction of classical shaded A-polynomials $A_a(\ell_b,m_c)$ for $SU(N)$; explicit $\mathfrak{su}_3$ A-polynomials for knots $3_1$, $4_1$, $5_1$; a connection between CG chords and Reeb chords in knot contact homology (for $\mathfrak{su}_2$), extending augmentation polynomials to arbitrary $\mathfrak{su}_N$ and representations.
AI.conclusion: The CG chord formalism provides a systematic route to generalize A-polynomials to arbitrary Lie (super)algebras $\mathfrak{g}$, both classical and quantum, with the double-scaling limit serving as a bridge between the two regimes.

title: Two photon decay width of the fully charmed tetraquarks: revisiting prospects for ultraperipheral collisions
summary: We discuss the role of fully heavy tetraquarks in ultraperipheral collisions $AA\to AA\, J/ψJ/ψ$ and $AA \to AA\, γγ$. Two-photon couplings to scalar and tensor tetraquarks are considered. We use relatively recent results of four-body calculation of fully heavy tetraquark wave function within the extended relativized quark model. The corresponding radiative decay widths for different tetraquark states are evaluated using NRQCD factorisation, with LDMEs extracted from the four-body wave functions at the origin. The results are collected in tables. The cross sections for production of pairs of $J/ψ$ mesons and diphotons in UPC of $^{208}Pb + {^{208}Pb}$ collisions are presented. While the couplings for $T_{4c}\left(0^{++}, 2^{++}\right) \to γγ$ are calculated based on the model wave functions, simplified couplings are used for $T_{4c}\left(0^{++}, 2^{++}\right) \to J/ψJ/ψ$. When calculating the energy dependence of the resonant $γγ\to J/ψJ/ψ$ and $γγ\to γγ$ cross section, we employ the total decay widths measured at $Γ_{\rm{tot}}=0.446\,\rm{GeV}$ for $X(6600)$ while $Γ_{\rm{tot}}=0.135\,\rm{GeV}$ for $X(6900)$ in latest CMS data. The resonant terms are compared with continuum contributions for both considered channels. While for the $J/ψJ/ψ$ channel the resonant contributions are larger than continuum ones, for the $γγ$ channels the situation is reversed. The latter result is in clear disagreement with the result obtained from the näive use of vector dominance picture.

AI.tldr: This paper studies fully heavy tetraquark production in ultraperipheral lead-lead collisions, focusing on their two-photon couplings and decays to J/ψJ/ψ and γγ. Using relativistic quark model wave functions and NRQCD factorization, the authors compute radiative decay widths and compare resonant vs. continuum contributions. They find resonant contributions dominate in J/ψJ/ψ channel but are subdominant in γγ channel, contradicting the naive vector dominance model.
AI.motivation: To investigate the role of fully heavy tetraquarks (particularly T₄c states) in ultraperipheral heavy-ion collisions and to test theoretical predictions against experimental data, especially the recently observed X(6600) and X(6900) resonances.
AI.method: The authors use the extended relativized quark model for four-body tetraquark wave functions, NRQCD factorization to extract LDMEs from wave functions at the origin, and evaluate radiative decay widths. They compare resonant cross sections (using experimental total widths from CMS) with continuum contributions in UPCs of ²⁰⁸Pb+²⁰⁸Pb.
AI.result: Resonant contributions to J/ψJ/ψ production are larger than continuum contributions, while for γγ production the continuum dominates. The latter contradicts the naive vector dominance picture. Numerical results for cross sections and decay widths are tabulated.
AI.conclusion: Fully heavy tetraquarks can be produced and detected via two-photon fusion in UPCs, but the γγ channel is not dominated by resonant tetraquark contributions as vector dominance would suggest; the J/ψJ/ψ channel is more promising for resonant searches.

title: Ising surface defects can get dirty
summary: Real critical systems, such as uniaxial ferromagnets in the 3d Ising universality class, are constrained by boundaries and subject to random couplings. We consider the Wilson-Fisher fixed point in $4-ε$ dimensions subject to a random magnetic field localized on a two-dimensional surface, which becomes co-dimension 1 in the physical $ε\to1$ limit. Using the replica method for the disordered field, we find that the ordinary boundary condition is stable under disorder but also discover a non-trivial ``dirty" boundary condition which can be reached by tuning the disorder strength or the local temperature. We also investigate the logarithmic structure of the defect spectrum and how it emerges via the replica formalism.

AI.tldr: The paper studies random magnetic fields localized on a 2D surface in the 3d Ising universality class using the replica method in 4-ε dimensions, finding a stable ordinary boundary condition and a tunable "dirty" boundary condition, plus logarithmic structures in the defect spectrum.
AI.motivation: Real critical systems (like uniaxial ferromagnets) are constrained by boundaries and subject to random couplings, but their combined effect is not well understood.
AI.method: Wilson-Fisher fixed point in 4-ε dimensions with a random magnetic field on a 2D surface (co-dimension 1 in ε→1 limit), analyzed via the replica method for disordered systems.
AI.result: The ordinary boundary condition remains stable under disorder; a non-trivial "dirty" boundary condition emerges and can be reached by tuning disorder strength or local temperature; logarithmic structure in the defect spectrum is uncovered via replica formalism.
AI.conclusion: Disorder on boundaries introduces new fixed points and richer boundary critical phenomena beyond the pristine case.

title: Emergent Neutrino Texture Geometry from Dark Matter and Lepton Flavor Violation in the Scotogenic Model
comment: 28 pages, 10 figures, 6 tables. Numerical analysis performed using Casas--Ibarra reconstruction and micrOMEGAs 6.3.0. The manuscript investigates emergent approximate neutrino texture structures, flavor geometry, and dark matter--LFV tension in the minimal fermionic scotogenic model
summary: We investigate the emergence of approximate neutrino texture structures in the minimal scotogenic model through large-scale Casas--Ibarra parameter scans subject to lepton flavor violation and dark matter constraints. We demonstrate that approximate suppressions can dynamically emerge from phenomenological consistency conditions. The interplay between relic density requirements, radiative neutrino mass generation, and lepton flavor violating observables induces a nontrivial flavor geometry in parameter space. Particular suppressions in the $(eμ)$ and $(eτ)$ sectors arise naturally, while diagonal entries strongly resist cancellation. We further compare normal and inverted mass hierarchies, analyze reduced versus full Casas--Ibarra geometries, and identify approximate scaling relations linking dark matter and flavor observables. Our results suggest that emergent flavor structures may represent dynamical consequences of radiative neutrino mass generation rather than externally imposed flavor symmetries.

AI.tldr: The paper investigates how approximate neutrino texture structures emerge naturally in the minimal scotogenic model from phenomenological constraints (lepton flavor violation, dark matter relic density) rather than imposed symmetries, finding that $(eμ)$ and $(eτ)$ suppressions arise dynamically while diagonal entries resist cancellation, with scaling relations linking dark matter and flavor observables.
AI.motivation: To understand whether approximate neutrino flavor structures can emerge dynamically from the consistency conditions of the minimal scotogenic model (radiative neutrino mass, dark matter, lepton flavor violation) rather than being imposed as external flavor symmetries.
AI.method: Large-scale Casas-Ibarra parameter scans of the minimal scotogenic model, subject to lepton flavor violation and dark matter constraints, comparing normal vs. inverted mass hierarchies and reduced vs. full Casas-Ibarra geometries.
AI.result: Approximate suppressions in the $(eμ)$ and $(eτ)$ sectors emerge naturally from phenomenological consistency, while diagonal entries resist cancellation. Scaling relations between dark matter and flavor observables are identified.
AI.conclusion: Emergent flavor structures may represent dynamical consequences of radiative neutrino mass generation rather than externally imposed flavor symmetries.

title: Bottom-up open EFT for non-Abelian gauge theory with dynamical color environment
summary: We develop a bottom-up open effective field theory (EFT) for non-Abelian gauge theories within the Schwinger--Keldysh formalism. Instead of integrating out the environment completely and starting from a nonlocal influence functional, we retain the slow environmental response variables explicitly and construct a local system-environment EFT. The environmental sector is described by a dynamical color-frame variable, Stückelberg-like field, and an associated color-current sector, which gives the nontrivial interactions and dissipation between the system and the environment. The resulting construction provides a gauge-covariant Markov embedding of nonlocal and non-Markovian color response. After integrating out the retained environmental variables with retarded boundary conditions, the reduced system theory acquires nonlocal dissipative kernels and stochastic sources. We show that the hard thermal loop response arises naturally as a particular realization of the retained environmental response. Our framework provides a local open-EFT description of color transport, memory effects, and fluctuation-dissipation structure in non-Abelian plasmas, and offers a systematic starting point for dissipative Yang--Mills EFTs with dynamical environments.
